input.question: Why do my ears sometimes pop when I swallow?

evidence.title: Sensory Perception — Audition (Hearing)
evidence.text: The middle ear is connected to the pharynx through the Eustachian tube, which helps equilibrate air pressure across the tympanic membrane. The tube is normally closed but will pop open when the muscles of the pharynx contract during swallowing or yawning.

answer.text: Swallowing can briefly open a small tube between your middle ear and your throat. That opening helps even out the air pressure on either side of your eardrum and can feel like a pop.

input.question: How does swallowing help equalize middle-ear pressure?

evidence.title: Sensory Perception — Audition (Hearing)
evidence.text: The middle ear is connected to the pharynx through the Eustachian tube, which helps equilibrate air pressure across the tympanic membrane. The tube is normally closed but will pop open when the muscles of the pharynx contract during swallowing or yawning.

answer.text: Contraction of the pharyngeal muscles during swallowing opens the normally closed Eustachian tube. This connects the middle ear with the pharynx and allows pressure to equalize across the tympanic membrane.
